scope: Make launcher claim/processing/activity atomic and publish an instance only while the same raw claim owns the sequence.

beforeAfter.before: Claim/activity committed before a separate unconditional processing write, so a write failure left a claimed slot/start activity and a replacement run could be reset to processing.
beforeAfter.after: The existing CAS UPDATE writes raw claim, processing and null statusError together. With activity, the existing D1 batch commits or rolls back all of them. No separate launcher status write remains.

beforeAfter.before: After creating a workflow, the launcher unconditionally updated the sequence workflowRunId and could replace a newer owner.
beforeAfter.after: publishWorkflowInstance matches sequence, organization and this raw claim in one UPDATE. A miss keeps the newer row unchanged but returns the created instance id. A hit preserves fast terminal state/error.

beforeAfter.before: The conditional start-activity insert checked sequence id and proposed claim without independently checking organization.
beforeAfter.after: The activity condition also matches the scoped organization; a foreign attempt that supplies the existing owner cannot write its activity.

preservedContracts: Acquisition CAS failure still refuses before workflow creation. Fresh claims retain their original deduplication identity and start-activity text.
The existing launch-time processing behavior and prior-error clearing now commit with acquisition. activity:null has no activity insert.
Publication returns boolean and never changes status/statusError. A miss does not throw, retry creation or mark the created run failed.
Real publication SQL exceptions still reject. They are not converted to ownership misses or false creation-failure events.
The internal workflowClaimId snapshot and prior failure guard are unchanged. No task payload, public API/MCP, provider routing, pricing or schema change.

productionCallSites.purpose: The only production claimWorkflowSlot caller. Reuses the acquired claim for dispatch, trigger-failure cleanup and guarded publication.
Returns the actually-created workflow id separately from the sequence row.
Collects the launched id for later observation.
Continue collects the launched id. getOperationStatus validates access and resolves the supplied instance, without requiring it to equal the current sequence slot.
withContinueSwitches rolls back only on an exception; an ordinary publication miss must not misreport the created workflow as refused.

callerReview.method: Read-only production call-path review. No caller requiring unconditional slot overwrite was found. The real Continue wrapper regression covers the no-rollback result with a mocked workflow engine; other caller suites still use their documented launcher mocks.

originalAssertionTreatment: The obsolete standalone processing and unconditional update call assertions were replaced by acquisition/publication contract assertions. Exact content/model/locale snapshots and active/unknown/lost-CAS rejection remain. Trigger failure cleanup variants remain covered in a parameterized test; original error identity, failure activity and no-publication assertions are retained. Publication miss and surfaced SQL failure are distinct cases.
alternativeAssessment: Outer guards or another mutable read cannot make the two launch writes atomic. Reuse the existing scoped CAS and D1 activity batch, then add one narrow publication method; no timing threshold, lease, scheduler, schema or duplicate workflow implementation was introduced.
remainingActions: Raw unpublished claims still resolve as failed/no_binding and may be reclaimed while the original create call remains in flight. This batch preserves replacement ownership; it does not prove strict root exclusion or cooperative cancellation.
Storyboard runImpl startup and success writes and analyze-script child failure ownership remain open.
Continue switch save/refusal rollback is not guarded against a competing request; independent Update all only prechecks processing and has no Storyboard slot claim.
A real publication SQL error after workflow creation still rejects under the prior launcher contract; outer recovery, reservation and settings consequences are not closed here.
Failure notification retries, swallowed adapter errors, run identity and history replay remain outside this database publication operation.
Real Cloudflare replay/restart, Workerd HTTP, D1 multi-instance concurrency, browser delivery, paid providers and wallet settlement remain unverified. GC-03/P3 are in progress; P4 has not started.
